title: Exact duration of a macrostep
statement: Let $W$ be a finite binary Turing machine, let $a,R\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be an input word over the schedule alphabet. For a base configuration of the schedule machine on $x$, suppose its guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$ and its unary tape contains a unit marker at coordinate $u\in\mathbb{Z}$. Starting in the macrostep-check phase with unary head at $u$ and guide head at $0$, after exactly $6R+8$ steps the machine is again in the macrostep-check phase, with unary head at $u+1$ and guide head at $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$x$ is an input word over the schedule alphabet
the base guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$
the base unary tape contains a unit marker at coordinate $u$
replaced:
Suppose the base's guide tape is the fixed guide of radius $R$ and its unary tape
holds a unit marker at coordinate $u$.  Then running the schedule controller for
exactly $6R + 8$ steps from the counter-test phase with unary head at $u$ and guide
head at the origin executes the entire fixed path of one macrostep and returns to the
counter-test phase with unary head at $u + 1$ and guide head at the origin.
